items.message: `_restore_masked` reads the target file at call time, but `Workspace.redact` was populated at read time; if the file changed between the model's read and its write, the mask-to-value mapping is built from the new file content, not from what the model was shown.

The `cases` tuple is built from the short-summary section of pytest output, but the parse loop over reversed lines may consume lines from that same section, causing a double-count or misalignment if the summary appears in both places.

The restoration test asserts `change.contents == original.replace(...)` but does not assert that the redacted form of the staged contents still redacts to the same thing, leaving the 'values never reach the model' property untested at the boundary this gate is supposed to hold.
